title: Audit: strong at owning your catalog, weak at running a gallery
summary: An audit of 0.1 against gallery software from Artsy, Artlogic, ArtCloud, Artwork Archive and Arternal found Open Gallery ahead on export, safe re-imports, privacy and cost, and behind on daily operations: no sale, contact, edition, consignment or hold records yet.
why: Matching incumbents field for field would not earn a switch. The audit points to three places where software alone could be an order of magnitude better, each needing the missing operations layer underneath.
detail: The three bets: turn photos, messy sheets and consignment PDFs into reviewed records in minutes, with optional on-device AI; let a gallery's own assistant query and update its catalog through a local connector while the data stays on its computer; and make one record drive every output, from tear sheets and price lists to the website and the Artsy file. Our own weak spots, measured: repricing 20 works takes about 80 clicks, a 10,000-row import preview takes 7 seconds and blocks the app, lists load full-size originals, and exports hold everything in memory, so large image archives cannot be exported yet. Competitor findings come from their public help pages; anything not found there is treated as unknown, not absent.
next: Run a structured critique session on the three bets, then start on sales, contacts and editions while looking for one gallery to measure a real catalog import.
author: Claude

evidence.label: 10,000-work timing: search 10-12 ms, import preview 7.2 s, site build 0.7 s for 3,334 public works
